Devon: Heads up — did a full pass on token-budget scaling across cards, found some weird regressions once we pushed kernel-selector v2.3.1 to h100 pools. Profiling attached below.

Mia: repro steps?

Devon: Ran the same workload (mix of chat/complete, avg len ~120 tokens, 60% streaming, 40% short completions) against A10/T4/L4/A100/H100. Used running job that flows through continuous-batcher + kv cache.

Yang: thanks. what metrics are you seeing?

Devon: For each card I collected: p95 latency, tokens/sec, max_tokens_per_batch estimate, observed kv-frag %. Quick summary: H100 p95 up +9% vs baseline, A100 +3%, A10 -1% (negligible), L4 +7%, T4 +12%. Tokens/sec fell on H100/A100 by ~8% and T4 by ~15%. KV frag increased on H100/A100 by ~14% vs baseline.

Andre: any change in batch size distribution?

Devon: Yeah, continuous-batcher created fewer large-token batches on H100 after kernel 2.3.1. The batch_count for >100k-token batches dropped 28% on H100, while small batches (<8k tokens) increased. Looks like kernel-selector prefers a slower kernel for large sequences now, raising latency and discouraging packers.

Mia: hmm kernel fallback path? selector logs show fallback to kernel "attn_v2_compat" for certain seqLen+head combos. Could be a cost-estimate regression.

Devon: Exactly. Selector trace: 
```
[selector] model=gpt-compat seq=2048 kv_chunks=4 prefer_kernel=fast_fused_v1 -> fallback=attn_v2_compat reason=cost_estimate(1.12)
```

Yang: KV fragmentation explanation?

Devon: With the fallback we observe more KV splits because the kernel path expects smaller kv-chunk sizes; continuous batching tries to pack more requests but gets split due to kernel alignment rules. That increases memory overhead and reduces usable batch token ceiling.

Andre: what are the current safe ceilings you're proposing per card?

Devon: Working proposal (after adjusting for ~15% kv-frag hitting H100/A100):
```
H100: max_batch_size=32, max_tokens_per_batch=340000  # baseline target 400k, scaled down for frag
A100: max_batch_size=16, max_tokens_per_batch=190000
A10:  max_batch_size=8,  max_tokens_per_batch=82000
L4:   max_batch_size=4,  max_tokens_per_batch=42000
T4:   max_batch_size=2,  max_tokens_per_batch=28000
```

Mia: Those numbers look reasonable as a temporary mitigation. We should also test increasing `queue_hold_ms` slightly to allow packers to form fewer large-but-sparse batches.

Devon: Agreed. On H100 increasing queue_hold from 8ms -> 14ms recovered ~4% tokens/sec in my runs, but increased tail slightly for single-request latencies. We need to balance SLOs.

Yang: Also try forcing the selector to prefer fused kernels for >64k-token batches in the A/B test. If we can override cost_estimate heuristics with a kernel hint, that might avoid fallback-induced kv-frag.

Andre: good idea. We can add a temporary kernel_hint in runtime config: `kernel_hint.prefer=fused_attn_v1` for seq>1024 and batch_tokens>64k. Run with perf-bot enabled.

perf-bot: CI perf job queued: run-id=ci-71422. Will run A10/A100/H100 profiles in parallel. ETA ~45m.

Devon: Notes from quick microbench: when we force fused kernel on H100, p95 restores to -2% vs baseline but memory headroom tightens. Need to ensure we don't OOM on worst-case kv growth.

Mia: So two parallel mitigations: 1) conservative per-card max_tokens_per_batch (Devon's table) 2) selector kernel_hint A/B test to avoid fallback. Also experiment with queue_hold bump.

Yang: Also open to trying dynamic token_budget_target that shrinks target when kv_frag > 10% (feedback loop). That lets the system self-throttle before hitting high frag.

Andre: let's capture the experiment matrix:
- baseline (v2.3.0 kernels)
- v2.3.1 (current)
- v2.3.1 + conservative ceilings
- v2.3.1 + kernel_hint AB (50/50)
- v2.3.1 + queue_hold=14ms
- v2.3.1 + dynamic token_budget feedback

Devon: I'll run the matrix on H100/A100 first and report perf-bot results. For A10/L4/T4 we can try smaller matrix. Also adding a regression test in perf CI to flag >5% p95 regressions on common short-chat workload.

perf-bot: run-id=ci-71422 completed. Summary: H100 AB kernel_hint variant improved p95 by 7% vs v2.3.1, tokens/sec +6%. Conservative ceilings cut p95 impact but reduced throughput by 3%. Queue_hold tweak recovered throughput but raised single-request p99 slightly. Full logs: https://perf.internal/runs/ci-71422

Mia: thanks. Action items?

Devon: 1) Temp roll of kernel_hint on H100 pools while we fix selector cost model (PR incoming). 2) Apply conservative ceilings from table for next 48h to stop regression spikes. 3) Add KV-frag-aware token_budget adjustment (small PID controller). 4) Add CI perf gate for short-chat p95 on H100/A100.

Andre: I'll file the rollout PR and the runtime AB experiment.

Yang: I'll own the selector cost model investigation.

Mia: I'll update runbook with mitigation steps and add a note on expected latency tradeoffs.

Devon: Great — thanks everyone. I'll post a short follow-up with the final numbers after we run A100 sweep. :thumbsup:
